text.p: Brazilian telephone company Telebras SA rose above a 12-month high Wednesday to stand out among American Depositary Receipts (ADRs).
Telebras was up 1-3/4 to 160, above a 12-month closing high of 159-5/8, in early trade that put it among the most active ADRs in New York.

The rise came despite a downgrade by Morgan Stanley Dean Witter, which cut Telebras' rating to outperform from strong buy. Analyst Luiz Carvalho said Telebras had reached a valuation level closer to those of its Latin American and global peers.

However, Curtis Butler, vice president in Lazard Freres & Co's emerging market group, said Telebras still remained a draw despite downgrades by Morgan Stanley Dean Witter and other investment houses recently.
"There are reasons why one should be willing to take profits after an appreciation of 100 percent in six months, but on a valuation basis it's still attractive," he said.
Telebras also has been boosted by local buyers, who are moving into equities from Brazil's fixed-income market as interest rates decline, he said.
Three Brazilian Senate committees start debate Wednesday on a bill paving the way for the privatization of the state-run Telebras system.
Among other active ADRs, Scandinavian Broadcasting System rose 13/16 to 22-1/16 and Danka Business Systems Plc fell 3/16 to 40.
Advancers led decliners 185 to 150 among 814 ADRs. Volume was 8.2 million ADRs traded in early morning.
ADRs allow U.S. trade of foreign shares.
